etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English peyne, payne, from Old French and Anglo-Norman peine, paine, from Latin poena (“punishment, pain”), from Ancient Greek ποινή (poinḗ, “bloodmoney, weregild, fine, price paid, penalty”), from Proto-Hellenic *kʷoinā́, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷoynéh₂ (“payment”) (whence also Proto-Slavic *cěnà (“price”)).

Doublet of peine. Compare Danish pine, Norwegian Bokmål pine, German Pein, Dutch pijn, Afrikaans pyn. See also pine (the verb). Partly displaced native Old English sār (whence Modern English sore).

definitions.definition: (now usually in the plural) The pangs or sufferings of childbirth, caused by contractions of the uterus.

quote.citation: 1951 February, Forrest H. Howard, “The Physiologic Position for Delivery”, in Northwest Medicine, volume 50, number 2, Portland, Ore.: Northwest Medical Publishing Association, page 99:
quote.text: When the pains are every five minutes and quite strong or the cervix is five cm. dilated along with regular and strong pains, the mother is given a block anesthesia of 1 cc. of 1:200 nupercaine, 1 cc. of 10 per cent dextrose with .05 cc. of 1:1000 adrenalin.

definitions.definition: (countable and uncountable) An ache or bodily suffering, or an instance of this; an unpleasant sensation, resulting from a derangement of functions, disease, or injury by violence; hurt.
(uncountable) The condition or fact of suffering or anguish especially mental, as opposed to pleasure; torment; distress

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XIV, page 22:
quote.text: And I should tell him all my pain,⁠And how my life had droop’d of late,⁠And he should sorrow o’er my stateAnd marvel what possess’d my brain; […]

definitions.definition: (countable, from pain in the neck) An annoying person or thing.

quote.citation: 2024 April 17, “Rural railways: do they deliver?”, in RAIL, number 1007, page 58:
quote.text: Today is match day, Grimsby Town are at home, and the ground is walking distance from New Clee station. So, visiting football supporters coming by train have to change at Grimsby Town [station]. That's a real pain.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, dated) Suffering inflicted as punishment or penalty.

quote.citation: 1629, Francis Bacon, An Advertisement Touching a Holy War:
quote.text: We will, by way of mulct or pain, lay it upon him.

quote.citation: 1690, [John] Dryden, Don Sebastian, King of Portugal: […], London:  […]  Jo. Hindmarsh, […], →OCLC, Act IV, page 105:
quote.text: Seb[astian].  […]  [M]y duty, then, / To interpoſe; on pain of my diſpleasure, / Betwixt your Swords[.] / Dor[ax]. On pain of Infamy / He ſhould have diſobey'd.

definitions.definition: (chiefly in the plural) Labour; effort; great care or trouble taken in doing something.
(transitive) To hurt; to put to bodily uneasiness or anguish; to afflict with uneasy sensations of any degree of intensity; to torment; to torture.
(transitive) To render uneasy in mind; to disquiet; to distress; to grieve.
(transitive, obsolete) To inflict suffering upon as a penalty; to punish.
(intransitive, India) To feel pain; to hurt.

quote.citation: 2001, Sarah Caldwell, quoting C. Choondal, “Waves of Beauty, Rivers of Blood: Constructing the Goddess in Kerala”, in Tracy Pintchman, editor, Seeking Mahādevī: Constructing the Identities of the Hindu Great Goddess, page 104:
quote.text: Oh my head is aching, oh Lord Damodara [Visnu], give me "kazhi". The neck is paining, oh Lord Kamadeva give me relief. My chest is paining, oh Lord Madhava, give me relief.

quote.citation: 2009, Nithyananda Paramahamsa, Bliss Is the Goal and the Path, page 124:
quote.text: A lady visited the doctor, a general physician and complained of a lot of pain. The doctor asked her where she experienced pain.The lady touched her right knee and said, 'It is paining here doctor.'Then she touched her stomach and said, 'It is paining here too doctor.'

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English payn (“a kind of pie with a soft crust”), from Old French pain (“bread”).

definitions.definition: (obsolete, cooking) Any of various breads stuffed with a filling.
